summary: Raising the latte price from $5.00 to $5.50 decreased revenue by $16.0 despite a small increase in total visits. The most damaging move was college students abandoning the shop: their revenue fell $51.75, while office workers gained $13.5 and trades workers gained $11.25. Walkouts increased by 6 and wait times rose 1.0 minute, suggesting price-sensitive customers defected to rivals, who captured 4 additional visits. The menu showed substitution effects—cappuccino orders jumped 11 while mocha orders dropped 8 and latte orders fell 3—indicating customers switched to alternatives or avoided the price increase entirely.
